data.body: Phase 1 RCA amendment from the full-suite reproduction. The five-second watchdog itself is correct, but `tests/_isolation.py` dereferences `subprocess.run` during the autouse `_no_repo_commits` teardown. Three existing tests intentionally monkeypatch `run` on a production module's `subprocess` reference; because every reference points to the same imported subprocess module object and the guard teardown precedes monkeypatch restoration for these fixture graphs, the guard invokes the test double and raises `TimeoutExpired` against its own `git rev-parse HEAD`. Focused runtime proof: the three exact nodes each passed their call phase and errored only at teardown (3 passed, 3 errors), with the traceback entering the test-local fake from `_isolation.head`. This rules out a real hung Git process and proves test-double contamination of the safety guard. Defect legitimacy: the repository-isolation guard is a suite safety boundary and must observe the real checkout independently of the code-under-test's subprocess doubles; existing guard self-tests are the authority. Expected repair: bind the real runner at the guard boundary so later module monkeypatches cannot replace it, while retaining the explicit five-second timeout and real blocked-Git fail-closed behavior. Tests under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py` and `tests/unit/test_store.py` are held-out RED oracles and must not be edited.
